title: What happened in AI — Sep 24, 2026
intro: LangChain dominated agent-tooling news, shipping LangSmith Engine v2's red teaming and automated testing, a session-level trajectory view, custom app building, and a 0.8 release of Managed Deep Agents — four features in one day — while Databricks shipped a CLI for running coding agents at production scale.

Security had a rough day too: a macOS zero-day let unprivileged code hijack Meta's Muse assistant via a single debug setting, and Apple moved photo provenance to the camera sensor itself. DeepSeek's revenue run rate more than doubled ahead of a planned IPO, and Google and Alibaba both pushed frontier-model updates.
highlights: LangChain shipped LangSmith Engine v2 in one day — red teaming, session trajectories, custom apps, and Managed Deep Agents 0.8 — the day's biggest agent-tooling drop.
A zero-day in Meta's Muse macOS client let unprivileged code abuse a debug setting to bypass the assistant's extensive permissions.
DeepSeek's annualized revenue run rate more than doubled to roughly $1 billion ahead of a planned IPO, alongside a new paper on the sandboxed harness that trains its V3.2–V4.1 agents.
Alibaba unveiled a full-stack AI push spanning new Qwen models, custom chips, and an agentic cloud platform.
Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar to general availability and a new Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS voice-cloning tool.
